sources.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

discussion.body: The hands-only frame is the detail that stays with me: the client's face is blurred, but the barber's manual skill is exactly what the camera is after.

Blurring the clients' faces keeps them out of the frame; it does not settle what happens to the worker. The open question is whether workers are collecting data for machines that will do their jobs, and a blurred face does not answer it.

items.title: A Bengaluru Barber Is Recording His Hands. Whether Machines Will Do Workers' Jobs Is Unsettled.
items.body:
Mohammed Ashim has cut hair and trimmed beards in Bengaluru for four years. Recently, the 22-year-old strapped a camera to his head to record his work.

The camera records only his hands and fingers; his clients' faces are blurred out.

The larger question is whether workers are collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs. Bino Paul, a senior professor at TISS in Mumbai, says it is too early to tell.

sources.title: Confucius

discussion.body: The ritual offerings are the strangest part: he was associated with transmitting the ancient sacrificial system and received offerings in temples in major cities.
Fair, but the modern philosopher is not the only lens that matters. The imperial Confucius was bound up with classical interpretation and the training of officials.

items.title: The Philosopher Confucius Is Partly a Modern Portrait
items.body:
The Confucius who appears as a philosopher is partly the product of modern cross-cultural interactions, according to the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.

In imperial China, he was identified with interpretations of the classics and with moral guidelines for administrators, and therefore with training the scholar-officials who populated the bureaucracy. He was also closely associated with the transmission of the ancient sacrificial system, and he himself received ritual offerings in temples found in all major cities.

sources.title: Gen Z candidates in both parties aim to tackle high housing costs

discussion.body: Beating an incumbent first elected before you were born is a great line, but a primary win is not the same as passing eviction protections.
The agenda pairs eviction protections with easier homebuying, which are two different housing interests. That may be coalition-building, or it may be a blurry message.

items.title: A 26-year-old beat a longtime incumbent first elected before he was born. He wants eviction protections.
items.body:
Eli Sabin, 26, won a three-way primary in New Haven, beating both a democratic socialist and a longtime incumbent first elected more than a decade before he was born. His housing agenda includes more protections against eviction and making it easier to buy a home.

Elected officials at all levels in the U.S. are overwhelmingly homeowners, which makes a young challenger's focus on eviction protections and would-be buyers a notable contrast.

sources.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted

discussion.body: A battlefield network where drones start losing their connection above 100mph is a strange kind of infrastructure: speed itself becomes a liability.
Trump's statement that Musk reversed the limits is a claim about what Musk did; the defence ministry sources say Ukraine is still recording Starlink issues.

items.title: Ukrainian defence ministry sources say Starlink problems persist after Trump says Musk reversed limits
items.body:
Sources within Ukraine's defence ministry say the country is still recording problems with Starlink after Donald Trump said Elon Musk had reversed limits on the satellite uplink. Those sources told the BBC that drones were being recorded losing their connection at 161km/h (100mph), hampering military operations.

Trump had denied instructing Musk to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had “put it back.”

The defence ministry sources added there was “currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted.”

sources.title: Was Charlie Chaplin's Tramp Un-American?

discussion.body: The better question is not whether the FBI was right; it is why an actor drew both a decades-long file and a theory that his films were anti-capitalist propaganda.
The bureau's worry is evidence of how the FBI read the films, not proof that the films were anti-capitalist.

items.title: Chaplin's Tramp was an icon of poverty; the FBI kept a file on Chaplin
items.body:
The Tramp was Chaplin at his most iconic: dignified and downtrodden in a penguin suit whose jacket was too tight, waistcoat too short, and trousers ballooning around his legs. A genuine hobo, the character was also, in Barbara Korte's phrase, an icon in the public representation of poverty.

The FBI kept a substantial file on Chaplin from 1922 until his death in 1977, suspecting him of being a political agitator and a possible communist. As John Sbardellati and Tony Shaw note, the FBI feared that the Tramp films worked as anti-capitalist propaganda.

sources.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4

discussion.body: A private key of 4 is less a secret than a shrug. Calling that encryption feels like calling a screen door a lock.
The shrug is fair, but the weak credentials let anyone mint certificates for any website or mail server. That is a lot of trust to hand to a number small enough to count on one hand.

items.title: eMudhra, the Certificate Authority With a Private Key of 4, Is Quitting TLS
items.body:
eMudhra, a certificate authority, says it is getting out of the TLS business after issuing eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server. One of those credentials had a private encryption key of just 4.

Chairman V. Srinivasan of India-based eMudhra Limited cited rising compliance costs and noted that the business generated just 1 percent of revenue. The company also said social-media amplification around the incident had brought scrutiny out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in its business.

sources.title: Odyscenes: The Twelve Best Bits of the Odyssey

discussion.body: The island is a trap with excellent staging: the reader longs to be there even as the place is called a trap or prison.
Excellent staging is still staging. A trap is a trap, and the reader’s longing says more about Homer’s technique than about the place itself.

items.title: Calypso’s Island Is a Trap Homer Makes Sound Like a Haven
items.body:
Calypso’s island is a haven of peace and beauty, and even the god Hermes takes delight in its wonders. It is also a trap or a prison.

Homer’s descriptions of beautiful places make the reader long to be transported there; the invitation and the warning belong to the same description.

sources.title: Why Quebec's strategic reserve of maple syrup is running dry

discussion.body: Processors appear to have bought out what was there, and when the reserve is low they compete for supply. That is less a raid than a scramble among buyers who can see the bottom of the barrel.

A reserve set up to try to stabilize supplies and prices becomes a different thing when it is low: competition to secure supply is the story. That is not a buffer smoothing a market; it is the buffer becoming the market's most contested asset.

items.title: Quebec's maple syrup reserve is running dry because processors appear to have bought out what was there
items.body:
Quebec's maple syrup producers set up the reserve in 2000 to try to stabilize supplies and prices, said Maurice Doyon, a professor at Laval University in Quebec City who specializes in agri-food economics.

This time, CBC reports that the reserve is running dry because Quebec's authorized processors — who buy, bottle, process and market the syrup — appear to have bought out what was there. When the reserve is low, they compete with each other to secure supply.

sources.title: Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine

discussion.body: The interesting bit is the boring promise that nothing else has to change: drop-in, no code changes, no new SKU. That is the feature teams actually budget for.
No code changes is not no QA. A voice still has to read back tracking numbers, addresses, and confirmation codes correctly, and that is a listening test.

items.title: Amazon says its Polly upgrade is drop-in for existing generative voices: 14 new voices, no price increase
items.body:
Amazon's Polly Generative engine has a new upgrade that the company says delivers more expressive, more accurate speech with low latency. It adds 14 voices across nine locales, including the first general availability of generative Hindi and Finnish voices, and is now generally available in production.

The practical pitch is migration cost. Amazon calls it a drop-in upgrade for existing generative voices and says no code changes are required. There is no cost increase, no new SKU, and no change to existing integrations, according to the company.

sources.title: How Rescale built an AI triage agent with Strands Agents and AI-DLC

discussion.body: An interview is a stranger first deliverable than a repository skeleton. If understanding intent is the bottleneck, 20 questions from the model is exactly where a build should begin.
Questions are cheap; the mob is what makes them count. Twenty questions answered by a room that has to agree on each answer is a different artifact from twenty answered alone at 11pm.

items.title: The Hard Part of Rescale's Triage Agent Was Getting the AI to Understand the Job
items.body:
Rescale's triage agent automates the classification and routing of nightly end-to-end test failures. In AWS's account of the build, the hard part wasn't writing code. It was making sure the AI understood what the team wanted to build.

The work followed AI-DLC, which AWS describes as an open-source, AI-centric methodology for software development. The engagement itself was a five-day, in-person workshop: AWS architects guiding while Rescale engineers worked hands-on-keyboard, co-building in real time. Working in mob format, the team answered more than 20 clarification questions generated by the AI before settling the scope.

Two architecture pivots emerged during the build, and the team validated each one before changing course. That is the detail worth keeping: the workshop was not a straight line from intent to implementation, and the discipline on offer is checking a pivot, in a room, before taking it.

sources.title: Traction!

discussion.body: The good part is the layering of hazards: fat grease between wheel and axle, the risk that sufficiently hot grease catches fire, and then water as the coolant. Every fix quietly announces that the previous fix was incomplete.

But the fat wasn't Rome's bright idea. The Sumerians had already worked out that fats and oils lubricate surfaces more effectively than water does; on this account, Rome's contribution is the cooling, not the grease.

items.title: Rome's Chariot-Wheel Fix: Animal Fat First, Then a Bucket of Water
items.body:
In the chariot races, the trouble was heat: friction between the wheels and the axle warming the surrounding parts, with the author imagining drivers complaining about their hot feet. Horace described chariot wheels glowing during racing in Odes, a collection of lyric poems, and scientists now explain that glow as the energy of motion turning into thermal energy.

Roman designers eventually found a way to temper the problem by packing axungia, animal fat, as grease between wheel and axle. That brought its own conundrum, since grease hot enough risked catching fire, so they added a coolant and splashed water on the chariots — the ancient equivalent of a pit stop.

What I like is that the answer isn't a fantasy of zero contact. It's a routine built around the contact point itself: fat on one side, water on the other, with the fire risk managed rather than abolished.

sources.title: Goodbye, James Gandolfini

discussion.body: Blankness is an odd quality to praise in a lead performance, and maybe that's exactly why the role keeps generating arguments: there is less to pin down than viewers expect.

I'd push on 'blankness.' The sharper claim is contradiction: seeing the mob boss in Dr Melfi's rooms was to see, and believe, a fusion of contradictory qualities that the piece says only the best, most workmanlike actors can offer.

items.title: The Guardian's case for Gandolfini: the only actor who could see past himself into Tony Soprano
items.body:
The Guardian's appreciation of James Gandolfini rests on a paradox of self-effacement: scored over with small parts and emptied of ego as an artist, he was, in its account, the only actor who could see past himself sufficiently to inhabit Tony Soprano.

That matters for how the show is remembered. The intimate world of The Sopranos, which the piece credits with changing television for the good, was written largely in Tony's eyes. It also credits HBO with refiguring the close world of French New Wave cinema for television, with David Chase's lens and Gandolfini's gaze drawing viewers in and, in its telling, giving a decade of extraordinary art such as Six Feet Under, Breaking Bad and Girls.

The line worth keeping is the fusion of opposites: Tony's blankness with his complexity, his faithfulness with his infidelity. A performance built on that pairing resists a single reading, which is why the argument survives repeated viewing.

sources.title: Where to begin with Billy Wilder

discussion.body: The melancholy is not a decorative mood; it is the cost of Baxter's bargain. He has forsaken his values for success, which makes the film's charm feel like part of the trap.

That may be too moralistic. Wilder believed the audience was never wrong, and the film's mass appeal pleased him; the melancholy can sit inside a popular Christmas package without turning the audience into accomplices.

items.title: The Apartment Is Wilder's Arguable Magnum Opus and a Melancholy Christmas Classic
items.body:
By the time Billy Wilder made The Apartment in 1960, he had worked in Hollywood for 25 years; BFI calls it arguably his magnum opus. The film is a romantic comedy anchored in the grim 9-to-5 of C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon) and his one source of joy, the woman who works his office elevator (Shirley MacLaine).

Baxter has forsaken his values for success, desperate to please his corporate superiors. The mass appeal of this Christmas classic pleased Wilder, but BFI argues that appeal belies the film's complexity and melancholy.

sources.title: Iran says 7 oil tankers damaged in Strait of Hormuz, and other Middle East news

discussion.body: The bypass pipeline is the quieter story: the strait matters less when some oil can move around it.
A bypass does not make the waterway irrelevant. Iran's state television is still reporting seven tankers attacked or mined there, possibly the largest single-day total since the war began.

items.title: Iran Reports Seven Tankers Hit in Hormuz; Aramco Says Bypass Pipeline Volume More Than Tripled
items.body:
Iran's state television reported Thursday that seven oil tankers were attacked or struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. It said the damage could possibly be the largest single-day total for the waterway since the Iran war began on Feb. 28.

Quoting a statement from the Revolutionary Guard's navy, the report said four of the tankers were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire.

The president of Saudi oil company Aramco said the amount of oil moving through a pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz has more than tripled.

sources.title: Federal bureaucrats grilled over decision to strip status from over 700 Innu in Quebec

discussion.body: The burden-of-proof detail is the story: a lawyer told senators the reserve was created only after Kichera and Matshiragan died, so their names would not appear on any official government list. The affected people are being asked to prove something almost impossible.
The official's defense is narrower: in the absence of evidence, she said she had no choice but to revoke the descendants' status. A rule can be binding and still produce an absurd result.

items.title: Federal Officials Defend Revoking Status of 738 Innu
items.body:
Federal bureaucrats Lori Doran and Claire Thie defended their decision to revoke status from more than 700 Innu before a Senate committee in Ottawa this week. The 738 people affected are all descendants of Christine Kichera and Adelaïde Matshiragan, two Innu women who lived in the 1700s.

The hearing was the first time federal bureaucrats from Indigenous Services Canada publicly explained the decision. Lawyers working for St-Gelais-Dubé and other community members told senators that the people affected were being asked to prove something that was almost impossible.

sources.title: Socrates in the Street of the Marble Workers

discussion.body: The fun is in how much weight a single scratched pot can carry: it identifies a house, while the philosophical birth certificate comes from Diogenes. Diogenes is the one who says Simon first wrote down Socratic conversations.

The archaeological part is sturdier than the philosophical part: marble chips are consistent with a sculptor's workshop. The claim that Socratic dialogue was first conceived there is the essay's interpretation.

items.title: A Scratched Pot and the House Linked to the Birth of Socratic Dialogue
items.body:
At one end of the Street of the Marble Workers, where it meets the Agora, sits the House of Simon. Archaeologists named it after Simon because they found a pot base scratched with his name.

Diogenes says Simon was the first person to write down Socratic conversations. The essay argues that this is where the Socratic dialogue was first conceived. The street's name comes from large quantities of marble chips found in buildings along it, consistent with what one might expect in a sculptor's workshop.

sources.title: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing

discussion.body: A trailer built from pre-production assets is a mood board, not a demo.
A mood board is still a promise. A two-minute montage can sell a tone without showing much of the game.

items.title: A leaked Mass Effect trailer shows what the cancelled game could have been
items.body: The next Mass Effect game, first teased in 2020, was cancelled alongside BioWare's shuttering. A leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe offers the best look at what it could have been. The roughly two-minute montage describes itself as in-engine footage from a small team using pre-production assets. In it, an ex-military officer in an N7 trenchcoat—similar to the one in the 2020 teaser—meets an Asari at a bar.

sources.title: The Sopranos on TikTok: watching HBO’s bizarre 25-second episode edits

discussion.body: A reunion would have been a victory lap; a TikTok drop is a stranger way to mark 25 years.
The first episode's TikTok is built as a trailer for the whole series, so maybe the point is an invitation rather than a summary.

items.title: For The Sopranos' 25th anniversary, HBO chose TikTok over a reunion
items.body: For the 25th anniversary of The Sopranos, a cast reunion was one floated tribute. It didn't happen: HBO put the show on TikTok, with Warner Bros beginning to upload every episode—not in full.

sources.title: RFK Jr. adviser Calley Means resigns amid growing MAHA discontent over lack of progress

discussion.body: The resignation is less revealing than the list of grievances behind it: food security and glyphosate regulation are concrete tests, not vague vibes.
Means did not say why he was leaving, so those grievances are context, not a stated cause. I would not turn a resignation into a verdict on the policy scorecard.

items.title: Calley Means Resigns as MAHA Voices Cite a Lack of Progress
items.body:
Calley Means, a top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a chief advocate for the Make America Healthy Again movement, resigned from his position with the Trump administration on Thursday.

In a statement, Means did not say why he was leaving.

Means said he leaves with tremendous respect for President Donald Trump and Kennedy.

sources.title: Can you ever really think what someone else is thinking?

discussion.body: The transfer picture is flattering because it makes understanding sound like delivery: if the thought arrives intact, communication has succeeded.
Common ground is less romantic. It asks whether speakers share information, not whether one mind has copied another.

items.title: Two Pictures of Conversation: Thought Transfer and Common Ground
items.body:
The idea that understanding rests on shared thoughts is an old one.

Augustine described signs as transmitting to another person’s mind what is in the mind of the sign-giver. Locke, in 1689, contended that language’s purpose is the transfer of thoughts or ideas from one person to another.

Stalnaker’s common ground offers a different image: information shared by the speakers in a conversation rather than a parcel handed across.
